sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
The path was flat for five years, with revenue still $42.4 billion in FY2022, before two step changes: 17.7% growth in FY2023 and 17.3% in FY2026 [F6][F7][F10][D280][D421].
The FY2023 step came from the Cerner acquisition, which contributed $5.9 billion of revenue, 11.8% of the year's total [S61][D604][P48].
The FY2026 step came from cloud infrastructure, as customers purchased infrastructure technologies and renewed cloud contracts [P17][P20].
Cloud Infrastructure revenue rose from $6.8 billion in FY2024 to $18.1 billion in FY2026, 26.9% of revenue [S90][S92][D643].
It contributed 13.7pp of the 17.3% revenue growth in FY2026, against 2.8pp from Cloud Applications [D645][D668][D421].
Cloud applications and cloud infrastructure supplied 16% and 84% of constant-currency cloud growth in FY2026 [P17].
Operating income grew 16.6% against 17.3% revenue growth, so incremental operating margin was 29.4% [F24][D422][D421][D442].
Diluted EPS grew 34.3% against 36.5% net income growth, with the diluted share count up 1.7% [F74][D425][D423][D438].
Operating margin was 30.6% in FY2026, below the 32.2% window median and well under the 37.6% FY2021 high [F34][D788][D787].
It slipped 0.2pp in FY2026 as operating costs grew 17.7% against 17.3% revenue growth [D433][D436][D421].
The cloud and software margin fell because infrastructure expenses rose to support cloud infrastructure growth [P16].
The largest move was FY2022, when operating margin fell 11.8pp to 25.7% on litigation charges and higher cloud, services and R&D expenses [D246][F30][P58].
Net margin rose 3.5pp to 25.2% as the effective tax rate fell to 28.4% from 39.2%, helped by $1.5 billion more stock-based compensation tax benefit [D434][F54][D407][D360][P9].
Operating cash flow was $32.0 billion in FY2026, 1.88x net income, but capital expenditures of $55.7 billion left free cash flow at -$23.7 billion [F84][D408][F94][F104].
Free cash flow margin was -35.2%, the window low against a 26.0% median, and capex ran at 7.30x D&A [D405][D792][D794][D410].
Operating cash flow rose $11.2 billion on higher net income and $4.6 billion of customer prepayments with a significant financing component [P6].
Capex rose $34.4 billion, part of the data-center build-out behind the $260 billion of additional lease commitments [P5][P1].
Net debt reached $97.6 billion in FY2026, 145.0% of revenue, from $81.4 billion a year earlier [D414][D415][D367].
That ranks at the 0th percentile of six software peers on net cash to revenue, against a -0.5% peer median [D815][D816].
Debt rose 39.9% on $42.7 billion of senior notes and $5.0 billion of mandatory convertible preferred, funding capex and dividends [D440][P7].
Buybacks plus dividends were $5.9 billion, only 95.0% of the $6.2 billion spent on buybacks and dividends in FY2017, as repurchases fell to $95 million [D416][D19][X155].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover only 1.3 years of the FY2026 burn, and $260 billion of lease commitments sit off balance sheet [D412][D419][P1].
Free cash flow was below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at -0.03x and -1.39x, against a 1.06x window median [D362][D409][D800].
Net cash fell from -$76.2 billion in FY2024 to -$81.4 billion in FY2025 and -$97.6 billion in FY2026 [D320][D367][D414].
FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K figure of $17.1 billion by up to 0.60% [F44][X20][R5].
Whether FY2027 capex falls below the FY2026 $55.7 billion level, which would lift free cash flow margin off the -35.2% low [F94][D405].
Whether operating margin recovers toward the 32.2% window median from 30.6%, or stays below it as infrastructure costs grow [D788][F34].
Whether net debt, now $97.6 billion, keeps rising as the $260 billion of lease commitments commence from FY2027 [D414][P1].
